title: Aurora Health - Incident Postmortem & Mitigation Review
header:
Date: 2026-11-13
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Meeting type: Postmortem follow-up / escalation
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Riya Patel (Redwood SE), Noah Kim (Redwood CSM), Marcus Lee (Aurora VP Eng), Priya Rao (Aurora SRE), Dana Ortiz (Aurora Security), Samir Gupta (Aurora Product)
summary: Follow-up on 2026-11-09 production incident that impacted inference throughput for Aurora Health customers for ~90 minutes. Discussed RCA (GPU OOM due to KV-cache miscompaction + autoscaler flapping), immediate mitigations (rate-limiting, pinning model variant, increase replica headroom), and long-term fixes (KV cache bugfix, autoscaler hysteresis, dedicated capacity options). Agreed next steps: deliver patch ETA 2 weeks, share load test artifacts, update runbooks and postmortem doc, provide SOC2/network diagrams.
transcript:
[00:00] Liam: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we know time's tight so we'll jump right in. This is Liam from Redwood, with Riya (SE) and Noah (CSM). Marcus, Priya, thanks for making time.
[00:18] Marcus: Yeah thanks Liam. Quick context — we had the incident last Tuesday 11/9 where our inference latency spiked and error rates climbed, about 90 mins total. We're mainly here to walk through root cause and the mitigations you proposed.
[00:35] Riya: Right, so we sent the preliminary postmortem yesterday; big picture from our side: two failure modes aligned — a KV cache compaction bug that caused effective memory growth on the serving shards, and the autoscaler reacted by killing and restarting pods which led to cold-start thundering herd. The combination produced OOMs on the GPU side and evicted workloads.
[01:02] Priya: To be clear — the OOMs were on the GPU driver / runtime, not on the node host memory? We saw the GPU processes crash.
[01:12] Riya: Yes, GPU process-level OOMs. The tensor allocator hit limits when the KV cache attempted a compaction during a heavy traffic window, and there was also a scheduling jitter. The autoscaler configured with a tight threshold saw transient pod CPU dips and scaled down, then back up — that made cold starts multiply.
[01:36] Dana: From security I want to note S3 logs and audit logs looked fine but we did need the network diagrams. We'll need the VPC peering setup and KMS key usage.
[01:47] Noah: We'll share that; Liam I'll add that to next steps.
[01:52] Marcus: What was the immediate customer impact? Errors were 500s and long tail latencies right?
[02:00] Riya: Exactly — 5xx errors mostly, latency P95 jumped from 120ms to upwards of 2.5s for a subset of routes, and throughput dropped about 40% for a period. A subset of long-running chat sessions experienced truncated responses.
[02:22] Samir: Right, product calls in the Firehose pipeline timed out which bubbled up to our UI. We had to roll back to a lower model size for some routes to keep things going.
[02:33] Liam: Ok let's talk mitigations. Short term we recommended (1) pin the model variant for high-volume routes to the smaller quantized variant, (2) apply stricter per-route rate-limiting during peak windows, and (3) temporarily increase headroom by bumping replica counts to avoid autoscaler flip-flop. Priya, did those get applied last week?
[02:56] Priya: We applied pinning and bumped replicas by 20% for the critical routes. That stopped the immediate OOMs. We left rate-limiting as a last resort but it's in plan.
[03:07] Marcus: The bump helped yes, but we need a more sustainable solution than manual replica tweaks.
[03:13] Riya: Understood. Long-term fixes we propose: patch the KV cache compaction to make it incremental and memory-aware, add hysteresis to autoscaler decisions and avoid scale-downs during compaction windows, and add a cold-start warmup path (pre-warming or using persistent model warmers). Also better telemetry for GPU memory pressure.
[03:37] Priya: That KV fix — what's the ETA?
[03:40] Riya: Our engineers estimate a targeted patch in 2 weeks, then a canary rollout, and full rollout in 4 weeks assuming no regressions. We flagged the KV-cache behavior in the repo and will send the PR link.
[03:52] Dana: Will that change any data residency or encryption behavior? We need to be sure KMS usage is unchanged.
[03:58] Riya: No changes to encryption at rest or KMS usage; it's strictly an in-memory compaction algorithm change.
[04:05] Marcus: For the autoscaler hysteresis, what knobs are you changing?
[04:09] Riya: We're increasing the scale-down stabilization window from 60s to 300s, adding a minimum replica floor for high-priority routes, and tuning CPU metrics to be a smoothed moving average rather than instantaneous.
[04:23] Samir: Any impact to cost with those changes? Aurora will pick up extra replica hours.
[04:27] Liam: We'll model the cost impact in the follow-up doc. If you prefer, we can propose dedicated capacity options (Redwood Dedicated) for predictable throughput — that avoids noisy neighbors and autoscaler churn but it's a different pricing commitment.
[04:43] Marcus: Put that in the options list. We want predictable SLOs; dedicated capacity might make sense for our payment flows.
[04:50] Priya: Observability — we need better tracing for the model-inference path. The existing logs don't show GPU memory pressure per model shard.
[04:59] Riya: Agreed. We'll add mem-pressure metrics exported from the runtime, and expose per-route tokenization and kv-cache hit/miss rates in Redwood Console's route dashboard. We'll also include more granular traces for pre- and post-compaction windows.
[05:20] Dana: From compliance, we still need the SOC 2 artifact package and the network diagram; and confirm SSO/SAML metadata for user access.
[05:29] Noah: We'll upload those to the shared secure folder today.
[05:33] Marcus: Ok let's cover communication cadence. We need a final postmortem doc with timeline of events, root cause, customer impact, and the mitigations + ETA.
[05:44] Liam: We'll circulate a revised postmortem by EOD tomorrow with the timeline and the links to logs and the PR for the KV fix.
[05:51] Priya: Also, for runbooks and on-call, we need a playbook entry that lists the immediate steps (pin variant, bump replica floor, enable route rate limiting, rollback to smaller model) with exact commands or Console clicks.
[06:05] Riya: We'll draft runbook steps and include run commands for both hosted and dedicated deployments — e.g., API call to set model variant, kubectl/console steps to adjust replica floor, and recommended rate-limit thresholds.
[06:18] Marcus: Can you also include a post-incident test plan we can run to validate the fix (synthetic load tests)? We need to run that in our staging before you push to prod.
[06:27] Riya: Yes, we'll share a load test harness, parameter sets, and expected telemetry outputs. We also propose a joint dry-run next Friday to validate the patch on a blue/green canary.
[06:40] Samir: One more question — any sign this is related to model weights or quantization changes?
[06:45] Riya: Not directly. We observed that the quantized variant actually reduced memory pressure; it was the compaction logic that was the culprit.
[06:54] Priya: There was one thing — we saw one pod spiking at 100% GPU for a period before crash; is there any chance of a memory leak in the runtime?
[07:03] Riya: We're instrumenting for that in the patch. We're adding periodic leak checks and will trigger alerts on unusual allocation patterns.
[07:12] Marcus: Ok, let's do next steps and owners.
[07:15] Liam: Action items: we'll share the updated postmortem (Liam, EOD 11/14), Riya will open PR and share ETA (Riya, 2 weeks), Redwood to share SOC2 artifacts and network diagrams (Noah, 11/14), Redwood to provide load test harness and canary plan (Riya, 11/17), Aurora to run staging dry-run and provide availability window (Priya, 11/20).
[07:44] Dana: Also add security review of the canary plan — we'll validate KMS and network access.
[07:50] Noah: noted.
[07:52] Marcus: Anything else?
[07:54] Liam: One last note: we'll include cost analysis for the autoscaler changes vs dedicated capacity so you can weigh options.
[08:02] Marcus: Great. Thanks team.
[08:05] Liam: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the doc and schedule the dry-run.
[08:10] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: some names mis-recognized (e.g., Samir sometimes shows as "Samir G"), occasional mis-heard terms ("KV cash" vs KV cache), timestamps approximate.
